title: Choose a principle for each feedback talk
context: You lead a small team and give each person feedback one on one.
question: Which principle fits this moment?

principles.name: Name the behaviour
principles.rule: The facts are not agreed yet. Say what you saw or heard, without a judgement.

principles.name: Ask an open question
principles.rule: The facts are agreed, but not the cause. Ask what got in the way.

principles.name: Agree the next action
principles.rule: You both know the cause. Agree who does what, and when you will check.

cases.text: Sam agrees the last two handover notes named no owner, and you have both found why: the new template hides that field. You are about to ask, "So what will you change?"
cases.looksLike: Your line is a question, so it can look like Ask an open question.
cases.decides: Sam agrees what happened and you both know why. Agree who changes the template and when you will check.

cases.text: Jo says, "I didn't interrupt anyone in Monday's meeting." You are about to reply, "From now on, let people finish."
cases.looksLike: "From now on" sounds like Agree the next action.
cases.decides: Jo disputes what happened, so the facts are not agreed. Say what you saw: who was speaking, and when Jo cut in.

cases.text: Alex agrees they talked over Priya twice in Monday's meeting and offers to wait until the end next time. Neither of you knows why it happened.
cases.looksLike: Alex's offer sounds like Agree the next action.
cases.decides: The facts are agreed, but nobody knows why, so the offer may not stop it next time. Ask what was going on.

cases.text: Maya's last two handover notes named no owner, and you have not raised it yet. Your planned first line is "Why don't you care about handovers?"
cases.looksLike: Your line is a question, so it can look like Ask an open question.
cases.decides: Nothing has been raised, so the facts are not agreed, and "don't care" is a judgement. Start with the missing owner names.
